description: Baseline permissions for the main window. The permission list is deliberately EMPTY and has stayed empty through Phase 1c-2b-2a, including the localized macOS menu that Phase 1b-1 expected would need the first entry. The previous value, `core:default`, was not minimal — it expands to the path, event, window, webview, image, menu and tray defaults, and the image defaults alone (`image:allow-from-path`, `image:allow-rgba`) would let a compromised renderer load a local image path and read its pixels. Nothing here grants the menu anything either: a capability governs PLUGIN commands (`plugin:…`, `core:…` included), and the frontend does not build menus — it hands the translated labels to this application's own `set_menu_labels` command, which Rust builds the menu from. `core:menu`'s permissions (`menu:allow-new`, `menu:allow-set-as-app-menu`, and the rest) are what a renderer that drove `@tauri-apps/api/menu` itself would need, and granting them would let a compromised renderer replace the application menu with items of its own choosing. This is not an argument: `src-tauri/src/dispatch_check.rs` drives all seven commands through the real dispatcher with this file and the shipped `tauri.conf.json`, and `a_remote_origin_is_refused` attempts all seven from a remote origin — its attempt table is compared with the names parsed out of `generate_handler!`, so a command added and not swept fails that test. This application publishes no ACL manifest for its own commands, so there is no permission a capability could name to let a remote origin reach one; adding a `remote` block to this file was measured and changes nothing. Every later phase enumerates the narrowest permissions its feature needs — never a wildcard, and never a `*:default` set.
